open_points.subject: Project and Customer revisions and times after erasure
open_points.text: “A Project and a Customer carry a revision” and “A Project and a Customer — the records that carry a revision — carry the instant they were created and the instant they were last changed” contradict M01’s “An anonymised project is a Project” whose “revision and every instant are gone”, and M04’s erased Customer whose “revision” and “recorded instant” are gone.
open_points.question: Do the revision and time invariants apply only before a Project is anonymised or a Customer erased, or must those surviving records retain revisions and times?
options: Qualify the invariants so they apply only to non-anonymised Projects and non-erased Customers
Retain revision, created instant and last-changed instant after anonymisation or erasure
Stop treating the anonymised or erased remnant as the same model
open_points.default_guess: Qualify the invariants; State 0’s “nothing else” rules make the revisions and times disappear.

open_points.subject: ArtifactPointer lifecycle when a project is deleted whole
open_points.text: “Durable, a record of its own naming its project (M01); kept after anonymisation (R0-62).”
open_points.question: What happens to a project’s ArtifactPointer records when the owner deletes the project whole rather than anonymising it?
options: Delete every pointer belonging to the project
Retain the pointers as records naming a project that no longer exists
Retain them under a separate tombstone or deleted-project remnant
open_points.default_guess: Delete every pointer belonging to the project, because the selected action deletes the project whole.

open_points.subject: AuditEntry identity format
open_points.text: M09 says the entry’s distinguishing identity is “its sequence number, minted by Registry”, while Identity formats says “Every identity Registry mints … is an opaque identifier with no meaning in its form. Its concrete format is a UUID” and lists only two further minted identifiers.
open_points.question: Is an AuditEntry’s ordinal sequence number an explicit exception to the UUID rule, or does the entry need a separate UUID identity while the sequence number serves only as ordering data?
options: Declare the ordinal sequence number to be the AuditEntry identity and an explicit exception to the UUID rule
Mint a UUID as the AuditEntry identity and keep the sequence number as a separate ordering fact
Use a UUID only and derive ordering from another fact
open_points.default_guess: Make the ordinal sequence number an explicit exception, since M09 already relies on it to distinguish entries.

open_points.subject: Audit sequence high-water fact
open_points.text: “then one more than the last ever written; never reused, also after old entries are erased”
open_points.question: Which durable model or instance fact preserves the last-issued audit sequence after the owner erases the entry carrying the greatest sequence number, especially after all entries are erased?
options: Keep a durable next-sequence or high-water fact outside the erasable entries
Keep a non-erasable audit metadata record containing the high-water value
Retain a tombstone for the greatest erased sequence
Permit sequence reuse after the relevant entries are erased
open_points.default_guess: Keep a durable audit-sequence high-water fact outside the erasable AuditEntry records.
